clue.text: Dr Rory, a Scotsman, doctored in old county

indicators.note: something doctored has been tampered with, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Highland tale of a Scottish doctor and his companion, tampered with somewhere in an old shire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dr' looks like a title but is just letters in the fodder. Ross and Cromarty was a county in the far north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ross and Cromarty was a historic Scottish county, abolished in the 1975 local government reorganisation.

clue.text: Cornish fare near ruin in old county

indicators.note: to ruin something is to wreck it, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cornish food served beside a ruined castle somewhere in an old county.
explanation.walkthrough: Caernarfonshire was a county in north-west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Caernarfonshire was a historic Welsh county, merged into Gwynedd in 1974.

clue.text: Badgering girl brought up with small notebooks

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the girl's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Sarah is a girl's name
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
note gives ME (a variant of mi, the note in sol-fa) and books gives NT, the New Testament

explanation.surface: A girl pestering someone while carrying little notebooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notebooks' splits as note + books: ME is the sol-fa note and NT the New Testament books.
explanation.definitionFit: Badgering, as a noun, is persistent pestering or intimidation, which is what harassment means.

clue.text: Spinster's game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an unmarried older woman, in dated usage
second meaning: a children's card game in which the player left holding the odd queen loses

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive suggests a game belonging to a spinster; the 's is just 'is' linking the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a dated term for an unmarried woman and the name of a card game about pairing cards.

clue.text: Wild beast's regular date in March, say

indicators.note: regular means taking letters at even intervals, here every second letter

explanation.surface: A wild animal keeps a regular appointment in March.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of 'Wild beast' gives the answer. The Ides fell on the 15th of March, as well as of May, July and October, hence 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the Ides were the middle day of a month, famously the fifteenth of March.

clue.text: Limits of council house register affected county

indicators.note: affected here means acted upon or altered, so the letters are rearranged
the limits of a word are its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: Council housing rules have had an effect across a county.
explanation.walkthrough: CL (the ends of 'council') joins HOUSE and REGISTER, and all of it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloucestershire is an English county in the west of the country, around Gloucester and the Cotswolds.

clue.text: Roles from Ken Loach film first televised in fact in old division of Lincolnshire

parts.note: roles in a play are parts
of can mean from, as in 'a man of Kent'
Kes (1969) is Ken Loach's film about a boy and his kestrel

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: even, as an intensifier, means indeed or in fact

explanation.surface: Acting roles in a Ken Loach film that was first shown on television.
explanation.walkthrough: Kes is the 1969 Ken Loach film; T is the first letter of 'televised'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincolnshire was once split into three administrative parts: Lindsey, Holland and Kesteven, each with its own council.

clue.text: Write down almost everything? Never

indicators.note: almost means the word falls just short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to notate is to write down, especially music
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone asked if they should record every last thing answers firmly no.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic refusals: 'Never!' and 'Not at all!' each deny something completely.

clue.text: Money bringing sorrow, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means we hear it said, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: dolour is a literary word for sorrow or grief

explanation.surface: The old idea that money brings unhappiness.
explanation.definitionFit: The dollar is a currency, a unit of money in the US and many other countries.

clue.text: European peninsula having its air polluted

indicators.note: polluted means contaminated or spoilt, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A stretch of coast suffering from air pollution.
explanation.definitionFit: Istria is the triangular peninsula at the head of the Adriatic, shared by Croatia, Slovenia and Italy.

clue.text: Fly low round southern desert

indicators.note: round means the outer word wraps around the others

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
to desert is to quit or leave

explanation.surface: An insect flying low across a southern desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb but is the insect; 'low' is the cow's call, not height.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosquito is a small two-winged insect, and flies are the two-winged insect order.

clue.text: Peruvian once driving right away

indicators.note: away means the named letter is taken off

parts.note: someone driving is in a car

explanation.surface: A Peruvian once took the car and drove off to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the native people whose empire ruled Peru before the Spanish conquest, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Now listening to Radio 4, say, with it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: having the radio turned on, Radio 4 being a BBC station
second meaning: alert, trendy and up to date

explanation.walkthrough: Radio 4 is a BBC speech radio station. The second sense is the informal one of being sharp and fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both having a set turned on and, informally, being alert and in the know.

clue.text: X-rays girders

parts.note: an X is a cross
rays of light are beams

explanation.surface: X-rays and steel girders, a two-word list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'X-rays' looks like the medical scan but splits into X and rays.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossbeams are horizontal structural beams spanning a gap, which is what girders are.

clue.text: Laughed at getting put away

definitions.meaning: first meaning: mocked or jeered at
second meaning: ate greedily, in the informal sense of putting food away

explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' suggests being jailed, but here it is eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is both to mock with contempt and, informally in Britain, to wolf food down.

clue.text: Spoke of politician with kind of wooden raft

indicators.note: spoke of means the word is said aloud, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: a Con is a Conservative politician
a tiki is a Polynesian carved wooden figure, so tiki describes a kind of wooden carving

explanation.surface: Someone talking about a politician and a wooden raft.
explanation.walkthrough: CON (a Conservative) is spoken, giving KON. Kon-Tiki was Thor Heyerdahl's balsa-wood raft, sailed from Peru to Polynesia in 1947.
explanation.definitionFit: Kon-Tiki is the name of the most famous raft of all, Thor Heyerdahl's expedition craft.

clue.text: Sink or swim at first adrift in old borough south of Perth

indicators.note: adrift means loose and wandering, so the letters are rearranged
at first takes only the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sink-or-swim situation for someone drifting near a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Kinross is a town south of Perth, once a burgh in the county of Kinross-shire.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinross was a royal burgh in central Scotland, a small town by Loch Leven to the south of Perth.

clue.text: Depressed, fusses about a place for servants

parts.note: to be depressed is to feel down

indicators.note: about means the word goes around the letter a

parts.note: stirs can mean causes a fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: A low-spirited servant fussing about the house.
explanation.definitionFit: In a grand household the servants' quarters were below stairs, in the basement, hence downstairs.

clue.text: Reckless prang — not chauffeur's first

indicators.note: not means the named letter is left out

parts.note: prang is British slang for a minor crash, especially in a car

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A careless driver's accident that the chauffeur didn't cause.
explanation.walkthrough: A prang is British slang for a small car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash describes acting hastily without thought for consequences, which is what reckless means.

clue.text: Degree status of composer with new role

parts.note: J. S. Bach is the classic crossword composer

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A composer's qualification earns them a new job.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is the holder of a first university degree, such as a BA, so it names that academic standing.

clue.text: Flee kitchen with food inside

indicators.note: inside means the answer sits within the words that come before it

explanation.surface: Run from the kitchen while carrying food.
explanation.definitionFit: The leek is an onion-family vegetable eaten in soups and stews, so it counts as food.

clue.text: Copies of the City shoe design

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: design means the letters are rearranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: Imitations of a fashionable shoe from the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoes are repetitions or imitations of something, as in a design that echoes another.

clue.text: Five have a good look round fast

indicators.note: round means the outer word wraps around the numeral

parts.note: to stare is to have a long, hard look
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five people take a good look around during a fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed, but it means go without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to go without food, which is what to fast means as a verb.

clue.text: Any rest unsettled Maugham, perhaps

parts.note: some can mean any, as in 'have you any?'

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A restless novelist given no peace.
explanation.walkthrough: W. Somerset Maugham was the English novelist, and in a puzzle full of counties Somerset also hides the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset was the first name the author W. Somerset Maugham went by, so it is an example of his name.
